input.step_by_step_reasoning: 1) Nodes: kept all whiteboard icons: the uploading user (entry point), S3, Step Functions, Elemental MediaConvert, Rekognition, Transcribe, Comprehend, DynamoDB, and the Reach Engine box containing EC2 and EKS (kept as two nodes because they are drawn as two distinct icons). The Lambdas mentioned in the audio are not drawn on the board; the board shows a direct Step Functions -> DynamoDB arrow, so they are recorded only in notes. The two step functions mentioned in the audio are drawn as a single Step Functions icon and are fused into one node. 2) Flow 0 (ingest and technical metadata): user uploads a file to S3, the upload triggers Step Functions, Step Functions kicks off the MediaConvert transcode to create a browser proxy, proxy completion returns to the state machine, then technical metadata (checksums, frame rate, media info) is stored in DynamoDB. 3) Flow 1 (AI/ML metadata extraction): Step Functions starts Rekognition, whose time-coded results go to DynamoDB; Step Functions then triggers Transcribe; the transcript text goes to Comprehend; the outputs of both Transcribe and Comprehend go to DynamoDB. 4) Flow 2 (ingest into Reach Engine): DynamoDB is a temporary store; once the data is there, an ingest into Reach Engine (EC2 + EKS) is triggered. 5) The DynamoDB -> Transcribe connection in the world model was dropped because neither the board arrows nor the audio support that direction; it is the Transcribe -> DynamoDB arrow.

graph.name: Levels Beyond: Media to Cloud Workflow for Reach Engine
graph.categories: Media & Entertainment, Machine Learning, Serverless, Video Processing
graph.notes: Levels Beyond's Media to Cloud workflow. A user-uploaded video in S3 triggers Step Functions, which orchestrates a MediaConvert proxy transcode, technical metadata extraction, and AI metadata extraction with Rekognition, Transcribe and Comprehend. All metadata lands temporarily in DynamoDB and is then ingested into the Reach Engine platform (EC2/EKS) for playback, search and visualization.

nodes.name: User
nodes.notes: Client user who uploads media files (essentially every video format) into the Media to Cloud workflow.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Bucket receiving user-uploaded video files; the upload triggers the Step Functions workflow.

nodes.name: Step Functions
nodes.notes: Orchestrates the video processing flows: kicks off the MediaConvert transcode, triggers Lambdas (not drawn) that extract checksums and standard technical metadata, then a second step function runs Rekognition and Transcribe.

nodes.name: Elemental MediaConvert
nodes.notes: Transcodes the source video into a proxy suitable for browser playback, giving users a visual check alongside the extracted metadata.

nodes.name: Rekognition
nodes.notes: Analyzes the video to identify celebrities, violence, nudity and other data clients want; results are associated with time codes.

nodes.name: Transcribe
nodes.notes: Converts the audio of the content into text.

nodes.name: Comprehend
nodes.notes: Runs analysis on the transcribed text to extract entities and detect things like when profanity occurs.

nodes.name: DynamoDB
nodes.notes: Temporary data store for video metadata: checksums, frame rates, media info, time-coded Rekognition results, Transcribe and Comprehend output. Once the data is there, an ingest into Reach Engine is triggered.

nodes.name: EC2 (Reach Engine)
nodes.notes: Part of the Reach Engine platform: lets users play back ingested content, view and search extracted metadata, see visual tracks of when each celebrity appears, and feed an orchestration engine to distribute content for monetization.

nodes.name: EKS (Reach Engine)
nodes.notes: Part of the Reach Engine platform, drawn alongside EC2 in the Reach Engine box: playback, metadata viewing and search, visualization and orchestration.

edges.notes: User uploads a video file to the S3 bucket.
The upload triggers a step function.
Step function first kicks off the transcode in MediaConvert to create a browser-playable proxy.
Proxy generation completes and the step function continues the workflow.
Step function triggers Lambdas that extract checksums, frame rates and other standard technical metadata and store them in DynamoDB.
After the basic metadata is extracted, another step function starts Rekognition on the video.
Rekognition results (celebrities, violence, nudity) associated with time codes are stored in DynamoDB.
The same step function triggers Transcribe to convert the audio to text.
Transcribed text is sent to Comprehend for analysis (entities, profanity).
Transcribe output goes into DynamoDB.
Comprehend output goes into DynamoDB.
Once the data is in DynamoDB, an ingest into Reach Engine is triggered.
Once the data is in DynamoDB, an ingest into Reach Engine is triggered.
